result.title: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
result.comment: 14 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the 10th Euro-China Conference on Intelligent Data Analysis and Applications (ECC 2026)
result.summary: Goal interpretation is to translate a natural language instruction into a formal symbolic goal that a planner can execute. It is critical for embodied agents because any error here propagates to every downstream planning and action step. Doing it well requires both generating suitable candidates and reliably selecting among them. We present a two-stage generate-then-rank approach to Goal Interpretation in the Embodied Agent Interface (EAI). First, supervised fine-tuning adapts a Large Language Model (LLM) to EAI's output convention. Second, Candidate-Output Ranking from Errors (CORE) learns preferences over complete outputs from the model's own generated alternatives. We conducted experiments on the household scenes of the Embodied Agent Interface Benchmark. Multiple open source LLMs including DeepSeek-V3 chat, DeepSeek-Reasoner, and Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-72B were evaluated. The proposed method outperformed the baseline models including LLMs with simple prompting, chain-of-thought, and knowledge graph based approaches.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究具身智能体的目标解释，即把自然语言指令转成规划器可执行的符号目标，提出先用监督微调适配输出规范、再用自生成候选上的偏好排序（CORE）选出完整输出，并在 Embodied Agent Interface 家庭场景上评测多种开源 LLM。
AI.relevance_reason: 方法线索是「生成多候选 + 按自身错误学习偏好排序」，可能为 latent 推理中的候选筛选、验证与「何时停止生成」提供可核查借鉴，但工作本身不含视觉状态或 latent 表示。
